title: Every lane the coordinator starts carries a cs-step tag, so the archive pass can see it
why: A lane with no cs-step tag never passes the idle-lanes archive tests: the build cannot tie it to a step. Example: #3052's lane session_013NEJKzMndrATd5V4pyEZoB. The same gap hid lanes from the stale-draft row on Nov 12 (plans/stale-drafts-2026-11-13.md).
note: The coordinator's lane start sets cs-step:<slug> with set_session_tags in the same turn as create_session. Guard: a check at lane start (or in the coordinator brief template) that refuses a create_session for a lane with no cs-step tag. Red test first. Until then, runner 10 archives merged lanes by the session named in each PR footer. Lane 01:23 CST Nov 13: #3111 handed in. Lane question (strict tag vs strip like guard_merge.py:1676) settled by triage, no owner item: a, keep strict; undoable, lane-recommended, the refusal prints the fix, and b widens what the check accepts. Note: the lane-start check and the archive guard read the cs-step tag two ways; a later change may give both one reader (rule building-one-home-per-capability).
